records.name: Merchant Guild
records.summary: Neutral trade houses that broker bulk exchange, credit, warehousing, and long-haul contracts out of secure market cities.

membershipModel.buyInRequirement: A substantial buy-in in silver, plus sponsorship from two standing members or a crown-chartered factor.
entryRequirements: Demonstrate liquid capital or bonded goods sufficient for a first season of trade.
Post surety against fraud, unpaid tariffs, and broken contracts.
Swear to guild weights, measures, and neutral market arbitration.
benefits: Access to bonded warehouses, caravan insurance, and guarded counting rooms.
Preferential access to long-haul contracts and bulk market auctions.
Use of guild letters of credit, brokers, and dispute arbitration.
memberObligations: Pay annual dues and civic levies attached to guild charters.
Honor guild tariffs, declared weights, and warehouse inspections.
Contribute guards, wagons, or silver when the exchange funds critical caravans.
membershipModel.notes: Large exchanges effectively operate as banks, customs houses, and trade courts.

records.name: Adventurers Guild
records.summary: Licensed contract houses for combat escorts, monster culls, ruin forays, patrol work, and other dangerous commissions unsuitable for ordinary laborers.

entryRequirements: Pass a live skills trial with weapon handling, field first aid, and formation discipline.
Complete a probation escort, patrol, or dangerous retrieval under a sworn senior member.
Accept guild arbitration for salvage shares, client disputes, and reckless conduct.
benefits: Access to vetted combat and escort contracts.
Use of guild notice boards, supply lockers, and casualty stipends.
Recognition papers that make travel, pay collection, and salvage claims easier.
memberObligations: Keep arms, armor, and camp discipline to guild standard.
Answer musters for emergency defense contracts when chartered settlements are threatened.
Submit spoil accounts and hazard reports after every sanctioned commission.
membershipModel.notes: Most halls sit near walls, ports, or caravan yards where danger contracts gather quickly.

records.name: Agricultural Guild
records.summary: Regional farming and orchard guild that organizes seed stock, field labor contracts, harvest levies, and bulk agricultural exchange.

entryRequirements: Complete a supervised planting, irrigation, or harvest task to local guild standard.
Demonstrate knowledge of seed handling, storage, and crop rotation for the local climate.
Provide a seasonal reference from a landholder, reeve, or chartered guild elder.
benefits: Access to seed reserves, shared threshing space, and bulk grain buyers.
Priority placement for seasonal labor contracts and emergency replanting aid.
Guild-backed measures for fair rents, weighings, and cart allotments.
memberObligations: Maintain clean storage, honest weights, and declared harvest shares.
Contribute labor or tithed grain to communal reserves in lean years.
Follow field quarantine rules when blight, pests, or flood damage spreads.

records.name: Fishers Guild
records.summary: Catch guild for river, coastal, and lake fishers that manages rights, landing space, net rooms, and auction order.

entryRequirements: Land, sort, and preserve a supervised catch without waste.
Demonstrate safe handling of nets, lines, shell beds, and tidal hazards.
Accept guild quotas, seasonal closures, and landing inspections.
benefits: Access to licensed waters, curing sheds, and catch auctions.
Shared repair yards for nets, hooks, baskets, and small boats.
Dispute mediation over grounds, moorings, and spoilage claims.
memberObligations: Respect closures, spawning protections, and storm recalls.
Keep guild marks on catch crates and pay landing dues.
Answer harbor musters when storms or raiders threaten the fleet.

records.name: Herbalists Guild
records.summary: A gatherers guild for medicinal herbs, teas, roots, blossoms, and other delicate botanical harvests.

entryRequirements: Correctly identify safe, potent, and harmful plants in a supervised field round.
Harvest and dry a mixed herbal bundle without bruising or contamination.
Show competence in recordkeeping for seasonal potency and gathering grounds.
benefits: Access to protected herb plots, drying lofts, and guild buyers.
Reference guides, remedy formulas, and storage standards.
Priority referrals to apothecaries, bath houses, and tea merchants.
memberObligations: Do not overharvest protected beds or sell misidentified remedies.
Keep accurate drying and potency records for guild inspections.
Surrender dangerous specimens for guild disposal when required.

records.name: Miners Guild
records.summary: Extraction guild for metal ore, coal, salt, stone, and other sub-surface or quarry resources before they pass into refining crafts.

entryRequirements: Complete a supervised shift with correct bracing, hauling, and spoil sorting.
Show knowledge of gas signs, bad stone, flood risk, and evacuation calls.
Carry references from a shaft boss, quarry reeve, or chartered mine captain.
benefits: Access to guild lease claims, haul contracts, and shared safety stores.
Mediated rights over shafts, drifts, and quarry cuts.
Burial and injury stipends funded by pit dues.
memberObligations: Observe guild safety signals, support rules, and assay declarations.
Declare productive seams instead of concealing them from the charter.
Contribute labor for rescue, collapse clearance, and water pumping when summoned.

records.name: Teamsters Guild
records.summary: Wagon and pack-haul guild that controls overland freight scheduling, convoy standards, and road-haul labor.

entryRequirements: Handle a loaded wagon or pack string through a supervised road leg without loss.
Demonstrate wheel, harness, axle, and cargo lash maintenance.
Know convoy spacing, night camp order, and emergency turnaround procedure.
benefits: Access to freight boards, relay yards, and guild-stamped cargo contracts.
Use of guild stables, wheelwright referrals, and guarded team yards.
Priority placement on crown and guildhouse freight runs.
memberObligations: Keep honest load tallies and declared cargo seals.
Answer convoy calls during famine relief, siege resupply, or emergency levy.
Maintain guild road conduct and animal welfare standards.

records.name: Drovers Guild
records.summary: Livestock-moving guild that manages herd routes, pasture rights, market delivery, and animal handling contracts.

entryRequirements: Complete a supervised livestock drive and pen count without panic or loss.
Demonstrate disease checks, branding protocol, and feed rotation knowledge.
Provide references from a herdmaster, market reeve, or drover captain.
benefits: Access to marked pasture corridors, market pens, and certified breeders.
Guild mediation over brand disputes, losses, and grazing access.
Priority booking for crown remounts and large herd movements.
memberObligations: Respect quarantine and disease notices.
Keep accurate head counts, brands, and delivery tallies.
Provide riders or beasts when emergency food or cavalry levies are called.

records.name: Rivermen Guild
records.summary: River and canal transport guild for barges, ferries, tow teams, wharf order, and inland water carriage.

entryRequirements: Pilot or tow a supervised river craft through current, bank approach, and load transfer drills.
Demonstrate lock, mooring, and flood-stage procedure where applicable.
Accept guild authority over landing order, tow crews, and ferry pricing.
benefits: Access to licensed ferries, barges, towpath crews, and wharf boards.
Shared maintenance yards for poles, ropes, hull patches, and lock gear.
Priority on state grain lifts and relief convoys.
memberObligations: Observe flood closures, toll schedules, and lock discipline.
Keep cargo tallies, landing receipts, and ferry fare registers.
Answer for rescue, bank repair, and barge salvage in declared emergencies.

records.name: Shipwrights Guild
records.summary: The chartered naval and merchant-vessel craft guild for hulls, masts, rigging contracts, and dockyard standards.

entryRequirements: Complete a supervised keel, spar, or hull-planking task to guild standard.
Demonstrate safe yard practice around cranes, saw pits, and pitch fires.
Present an apprenticeship mark or equivalent masterwork witness.
benefits: Access to drydock queues, timber allotments, and naval bids.
Shared lofting patterns, rigging tables, and yard labor boards.
Arbitration over refits, launch damage, and charter disputes.
memberObligations: Maintain guild dimensions, timber marks, and seaworthiness standards.
Answer harbor emergency calls for hull patching or storm recovery.
Train apprentices according to guild ratios in chartered yards.

records.name: Smiths Guild
records.summary: A broad metalcraft guild that governs smelting, refining, casting, forging, and finishing of all metals and alloys after extraction.

entryRequirements: Smelt and finish a supervised batch to declared purity and yield.
Forge, cast, or repair a standard guild test piece without hidden flaws.
Demonstrate understanding of fuel use, slag handling, and alloy proportions.
benefits: Access to guild assay marks, furnace standards, and master tool patterns.
Priority on military, civic, and infrastructure contracts.
Shared charcoal, flux, and emergency repair pools during shortages.
memberObligations: Do not misstamp alloys or dilute declared metal stock.
Maintain safe furnace practice and apprentice oversight.
Contribute labor during emergency arms, bridgework, or civic repair calls.

records.name: Woodwrights Guild
records.summary: A broad woodcraft guild that governs timber conversion, joinery, furniture, charcoaling, wood fuel finishing, and structural carpentry after felling.

entryRequirements: Dress a supervised timber batch into sound boards, beams, or fittings.
Complete a basic joinery or furniture test piece to guild tolerances.
Demonstrate safe use of saw pits, drying racks, and charcoal clamps.
benefits: Access to seasoned timber allotments, yard space, and guild buyers.
Use of shared patterns, work standards, and structural tables.
Priority on civic framing, shipyard joinery, and furniture contracts.
memberObligations: Respect timber grading, seasoning marks, and charcoal yield declarations.
Maintain yard safety and kiln discipline.
Answer major reconstruction calls after fire, flood, or siege damage.

records.name: Masons Guild
records.summary: A stoneworking guild that governs cut stone, masonry, carving, road setwork, and finished structural stone after quarry extraction.

entryRequirements: Dress and lay a supervised cut-stone section true to line and weight.
Demonstrate safe lifting, scaffolding, and mortar preparation.
Present an apprenticeship mark or accepted master witness for finished work.
benefits: Access to cut-stone orders, civic works, and master layout tables.
Shared lifting tackle, yard cranes, and mortar standards.
Arbitration over contracts involving wall failures, defects, or delayed delivery.
memberObligations: Observe guild tolerances for bearing walls, arches, and pavements.
Maintain scaffolds, hoists, and yard discipline.
Answer emergency repair calls after quake, flood, or siege damage.

records.name: Gemcutters Guild
records.summary: The finishing guild for sorting, cutting, polishing, and mounting gem stock after miners and traders bring rough stones to market.

entryRequirements: Grade and cut a supervised rough stone without catastrophic loss.
Demonstrate polishing, flaw reading, and honest assay practice.
Submit a finished piece or accepted master reference.
benefits: Access to secure cutting rooms, elite buyers, and assay seals.
Guild arbitration over flawed stones, valuation, and mounting claims.
Protection for luxury cargoes when routed through chartered exchanges.
memberObligations: Do not substitute stones, falsify weights, or conceal flaws.
Maintain security discipline around cutting rooms and ledgers.
Honor guild assay tables and declared valuation bands.

records.name: Textile Guild
records.summary: A clothcraft guild that governs spinning, weaving, fulling, dye finishing, tailoring supply, and other finished textile trades.

entryRequirements: Produce a supervised length of cloth or finishing batch to stated quality.
Demonstrate correct handling of loom tension, spinning consistency, or fulling sequence.
Accept guild inspection for dyes, shrinkage, and fiber substitutions.
benefits: Access to shared looms, fulling spaces, dye vats, and cloth buyers.
Guild marks for quality, origin, and contract compliance.
Priority on uniform, sailcloth, and noble-house orders.
memberObligations: Do not adulterate fiber lots or misstate weave quality.
Maintain dye-house safety and clean finishing practice.
Train apprentices within guild ratios and inspection windows.

records.name: Glassworkers Guild
records.summary: The furnace craft guild for vessels, panes, lenses, glazing, and all finished glass goods after sand and ash are prepared.

entryRequirements: Complete a supervised glass batch or vessel without devitrification or major flaws.
Demonstrate furnace discipline, annealing, and shard safety.
Show competency in color, clarity, and thickness control.
benefits: Access to furnace schedules, annealing space, and protected sand contracts.
Shared formulas for common vessel, pane, and laboratory work.
Priority placement on civic glazing and university commissions.
memberObligations: Maintain kiln safety and correct disposal of damaged batches.
Honor guild clarity grades and declared material quality.
Contribute to emergency replacement of civic glass after riots, storms, or siege.

records.name: Potters Guild
records.summary: A broad claycraft guild covering pottery, brick, roof tile, fired ceramic vessels, and other kiln-baked earthen goods.

entryRequirements: Throw, mold, or fire a supervised batch without major warping or kiln loss.
Demonstrate clay tempering, drying, and stacking discipline.
Accept guild grading of vessels, bricks, and tile lots.
benefits: Access to kilns, molds, storage yards, and civic brick contracts.
Shared glaze notes, firing calendars, and clay buyers.
Guild support during kiln failures or fuel shortages.
memberObligations: Keep kiln logs and declared batch counts.
Maintain safe firing practice and smoke discipline near settlements.
Honor guild standards for brick size, tile pitch, and vessel integrity.

records.name: Scribes Guild
records.summary: A records and factors guild that handles ledgers, charters, contracts, copying, and the administrative paper trail behind commerce and rule.

entryRequirements: Produce a legible ledger or charter copy without arithmetic or transcription fault.
Demonstrate archival handling, seal protocol, and record indexing.
Swear to confidentiality, accurate tallying, and anti-fraud rules.
benefits: Access to contract tables, copying halls, and archive rooms.
Recognition seals for ledgers, tax rolls, and official copies.
Stable work from courts, guilds, ports, and merchant exchanges.
memberObligations: Do not alter sealed records or conceal debts.
Maintain copying accuracy and secure storage standards.
Answer emergency musters for census, levy, or relief accounting when required.
